tally_frames.method: tools/vfull.py UNMODIFIED: load() + consumed_words() (word16 = (byte1 << 8) | byte3, raster order, GBP-VID-003); background = the word at pixel (0,0); a pixel is lit when |lum - lum(bg)| > 20 with lum = R+G+B of the 5-bit fields (bits 14-10, 9-5, 4-0); the checker's tally field `%2d` at console column 22 (8x8 cells; rows 4..13 = L, R, UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT, START, SELECT, A, B, from the checker's source); a cell is read ONLY by exact match against the glyph table below, transcribed from the frames; an unknown bitmap aborts the reading
tally_frames.walk_order_visible: the partial samples show the counters advancing in the declared walk order (L, R, then the run's four)
tally_frames.classification: FACT (data, recomputable): the preserved OGBPFULL1 frames of this run show the checker's tally screen with counts equal to the walk's arithmetic expectation, L = 1 and R = 2, reproducible from the archived file with the frozen parser -- NOT operator observation. The frames do not record which GameCube button was pressed.
tally_frames.blank_vs_zero: §V7.1.9 says an unpressed counter `reads 0`; the instrument prints a tally only on a press (updateButtonTally after keysDown), so an unpressed counter is BLANK -- read here as `never incremented`, the substance of the gate; the wording mismatch is recorded, not smoothed over

truncated_line.affects: the ENVINPUT record's last two fields only: the descriptor's status label (a constant of the format string, `CORROBORATED_not_FACT`) and `selftest=1` (repeated verbatim in the INPUT record); every other record is complete (the next longest payload is STARTUPT at 218); the four binary sidecars are unaffected; no gate figure is derived from the clipped fields
truncated_line.gate_reading: the §V7.1.8 IDENTITY / LOG line asks truncated=0 and the summary records complete: the ENVINPUT record is the one incomplete record, its lost fields are recoverable from the format and the INPUT record, and the INPUT machine gate reads from INPUT / INPUTT, which are complete -- recorded as the honesty item Issue #24 names, not smoothed over; the Orchestrator's classification stands
